evals.name: add-column-through-mcp
evals.prompt: Using the Screenplay MCP against a scratch copy of the canonical ScreenComposition corpus, add a priority column to the WorkItemList table. List the exact MCP tool calls in order and what you check before and after applying. Do not write files.
evals.expected_output: open-workspace to capture the revision and catalog revision, discovery through syntax-schema or the document reads, a proposal through propose-source or propose-ast, read-proposal before applying, apply with the matching expected revision and catalog revision, and a final open-workspace that confirms executable readiness.
assertions: Opens the workspace first and records both the workspace revision and the catalog revision.
Proposes the change through a propose tool and reads the proposal before applying it.
Applies with the matching expectedRevision and expectedCatalogRevision.
Reopens or re-validates afterwards and reports executable readiness separately from source validity.
Works on a scratch copy and does not hand-edit the .play files.

evals.name: stale-revision-recovery
evals.prompt: An apply call on the Screenplay MCP returned StaleRevision: reopen the workspace before continuing. Explain what you do next and what you must not do.
evals.expected_output: Reopen the workspace, read what changed, re-propose against the new revision and apply only with the new matching revisions; never force the old proposal through or bypass the check by editing files directly.
assertions: Treats StaleRevision as a fail-closed refusal, not a transient error to retry unchanged.
Reopens the workspace and re-proposes against the new revision.
Refuses to bypass the revision check by editing the .play files directly.

evals.name: comment-preservation
evals.prompt: We keep design notes as comments in application.play. Explain whether an MCP source replacement keeps them, which formatting option the server requires, and how you would prove it before trusting it.
evals.expected_output: propose-source requires CanonicalizeTouchedDocuments for typed source edits; prove comment survival by applying on a scratch copy, reopening the workspace and checking the comment on disk.
assertions: Names CanonicalizeTouchedDocuments as the formatting option the server requires for a typed source replacement.
Proves the behavior on a scratch copy rather than on the team's model.
Checks the comment on disk after apply and a reopened workspace.
